Subject: Pilot sizing ask: 70B model @ 32k context (KV cache + quantization)

Hi Michael / Priyom,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We're trying to scope the Dedicated pilot so procurement can budget the right GPU commitment. High level: we'll run an internal classification pipeline using the Llama-3-70B variant with 32k context and a mix of short (40-200 token) and long (5k-25k token) requests. Target traffic for pilot: ~80 sustained RPS average per model variant, spikes to ~200 RPS for a few hours/day.

Questions we need answered to a one-pager for finance:
- Rough GPU types + counts for reserved capacity (prefer cost-efficient and predictable latency).
- Expected per-GPU memory breakdown: model weights, KV cache headroom by token, and extra headroom for batching.
- Impact of quantization options (fp16 -> int8/nf4) on memory and expected quality for classification/regression tasks.
- Anything that changes if we enable prefix caching for repeated prompts.

We have a tentative 8-week pilot window starting Aug 1. Can you send a short sizing matrix and call out any hard limits or procurement blockers?

Attachments: delta_mru_estimate.csv (sample token distribution)

Best,
Jana Kovac

Subject: RE: Pilot sizing ask: 70B model @ 32k context (KV cache + quantization)

On Mon, Jul 9, 2028 at 11:05 AM Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwoodinference.com> wrote:
> Priyom / Soojin: can you take lead on the model-specific memory mapping...

Attached is a compact matrix (sizing_matrix.pdf) and a short set of guidance. TL;DR recommendations for Delta Pilot (80 sustained RPS, 200 spike):

- Model: Llama-3-70B-ish (baseline weights)
  - fp16 weights: ~35 GB compressed on GPU, runtime working set ~40–44 GB including optimizer/KV pointers.
  - nf4/int8 quant (post-training quant): weights down to ~18–20 GB; runtime working set ~24–28 GB. Expect modest drop in calibration/edge-case recall for classification (~0.5–2% AUC depending on prompts).

- KV cache sizing (32k context): ~0.6–0.9 bytes per token per key/value pair (model/arch dependent). For our tests with this model family: 32k context ~= 20–24 GB KV per concurrent full-context session.
  - If most requests are short (40–200 tokens) we can apply prefix/KV caching for repeated prompts to cut average KV footprint by ~40–60% depending on hit rate.

- Headroom / batching multiplier: for sustained 80 RPS with 95th latency SLO target, recommend reserve 1.4x per-GPU headroom for batching and spikes. For heavy long-context workloads assume 1.8x to allow for KV growth and concurrency variance.

- GPU picks / pod configs (illustrative):
  - H100-80GB: 1 GPU can host quantized variant + moderate KV if we shard KV off to NVMe for tails; recommended starting placement = 12 H100s reserved (gives ~16–20 concurrent long-context sessions depending on batching).
  - A100-80GB: cheaper for fp16; suggested 16 GPUs reserved for baseline fp16 pilot.
  - 4x A10 pod (32–40GB per GPU effective): lower unit cost but more complex orchestration; recommended for nf4 at production scale.

- Recommendation for Delta Pilot: start with mixed reserved pool: 8 A100-80GB (fp16) + 8 H100-80GB (for long-context heavy routing + quantized fallbacks). Enable KV prefix caching and a quantized nf4 model variant for lower-cost routing for short queries.

- Procurement notes:
  - If Delta requires hard latency SLA for tails, prefer H100s and increase headroom to 1.8–2.0x.
  - Quantization reduces reserved GPU count materially but expect a short QA window to validate classification fidelity.

I attached the sizing_matrix.pdf with the per-GPU worksheet and per-token KV estimates. Marissa, can you add a short line-item estimate for committed monthly cost (approx) based on the above mix?

—Priyom
Attachments: sizing_matrix.pdf

Thanks — this is exactly the level of detail we needed. A couple quick clarifications before procurement: 

1) For the mixed pool you recommend, how do you expect routing to behave? Will short queries automatically get routed to the quantized variant? Any code/ops work on our side to enable that?
2) For classification fidelity: the 0.5–2% AUC hit range — is that your internal benchmark or based on public studies? We need this framed for our ML lead.
3) Can you confirm if enabling prefix caching requires any changes to our request patterns or tokens to be sent?

If we can get that language, procurement is fine with the proposed counts and will draft the PO. We also want the HubSpot deal updated with the expected committed monthly baseline so the finance team can model it.

Best,
Jana

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jana Kovac <jana.kovac@delta-nanotech.com>
Cc: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwoodinference.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Jul 2028 16:03:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Pilot sizing ask: 70B model @ 32k context (KV cache + quantization)

Hi Jana — quick answers inline and next steps.

On routing: we recommend policy-based routing at the Redwood layer. Typical config we provide: short query route -> nf4/int8 quantized variant (cost-optimized) with automatic fallthrough to fp16 canonical model if confidence < threshold or latency SLO not met. No code changes required on your side beyond tagging request intent ("classification" vs "search") if you want route-by-task; we can also route by token-length heuristics.

On the 0.5–2% AUC impact: this is our internal benchmark across 5 classification datasets we run during model onboarding. We surface a dataset-by-dataset delta in the onboarding report. For many tasks the delta is <1% but for very edge-case, token-order sensitive tasks the gap can approach 2%. We will run a quick A/B on one of your sample datasets during the pilot validation week to provide a precise number.

On prefix caching: to use prefix/KV caching effectively you should send the full prompt for the cached prefix once; subsequent calls can reference the cache key. We'll share a short SDK snippet; no heavy infra changes needed.

Next steps:
- We'll post the finalized sizing matrix and a monthly committed cost estimate to the HubSpot deal (link below) by EOD tomorrow.
- Proposed pilot acceptance: Aug 1 start, 8-week window, joint validation at week 2 and week 6.

HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/4321/DN-2028-048

—Soojin Lee
